title: Precious Endgame: The Promotion Finish
summary: A pawn capture gains the tempo needed to promote, then the opponent’s own queen and pawn help form a mating cage.

nodes.question: Can the promotion race end with something stronger than a queen trade?
nodes.explanation: Begin after ...Qxc6. White has Ka7 and pawns d5/d2 against Ka5, Qc6 and pawns a4/b4. Capturing the queen with the pawn creates a passer on c6.

branches.title: Race to promotion, then use the mating cage
commentary: Begin after ...Qxc6. White has Ka7 and pawns d5/d2 against Ka5, Qc6 and pawns a4/b4. Capturing the queen with the pawn creates a passer on c6.
dxc6 captures the queen and creates a passed pawn already on the sixth rank.
b3 starts the opposing promotion race. This is the selected source continuation.
c7 advances one square from promotion while Ka7 supports its route.
b2 keeps pace with White’s passer.
c8=Q creates the queen needed for the coming checking sequence.
b1=Q promotes too. Count concrete checks rather than concluding that equal queens must draw.
Qc5+ checks Ka5 along the fifth rank and forces Black to address the check.
Qb5 interposes the new queen, using the king to protect it.
Qc7+ changes the checking angle. The black king must choose a new response.
Kb4 steps toward the center, but Black’s own a4 pawn and Qb5 block two important flights.
Qc3# checks diagonally. The d2 pawn protects the queen on c3, so the king cannot capture it. The queen controls a3, b3, c4, c5 and a5; Black’s own pawn and queen occupy a4 and b5.

branches.title: Independent final queen interposition
commentary: Begin after ...Qxc6. White has Ka7 and pawns d5/d2 against Ka5, Qc6 and pawns a4/b4. Capturing the queen with the pawn creates a passer on c6.
dxc6 captures the queen and creates a passed pawn already on the sixth rank.
b3 starts the opposing promotion race. This is the selected source continuation.
c7 advances one square from promotion while Ka7 supports its route.
b2 keeps pace with White’s passer.
c8=Q creates the queen needed for the coming checking sequence.
b1=Q promotes too. Count concrete checks rather than concluding that equal queens must draw.
Qc5+ checks Ka5 along the fifth rank and forces Black to address the check.
Qb5 interposes the new queen, using the king to protect it.
Qc7+ changes the checking angle. The black king must choose a new response.
Qb6+ interposes with check. Although Ka5 protects b6, White can capture there because Ka7 protects the capturing queen.
Qxb6# removes the interposing queen with mate. Ka7 protects b6 and a6, while Qb6 controls b5 and b4 and Black’s pawn occupies a4.

branches.title: Independent knight promotion misses the queen attack
commentary: Begin after ...Qxc6. White has Ka7 and pawns d5/d2 against Ka5, Qc6 and pawns a4/b4. Capturing the queen with the pawn creates a passer on c6.
dxc6 reaches the supported pawn race.
b3 advances the black passer.
c7 brings White one step from promotion.
b2 brings Black one step from promotion.
c8=N gives up the queen-based checking plan. The exact resulting position is losing for White.
b1=Q completes Black’s promotion. White’s knight cannot reproduce the queen’s mating attack, and this exact ending is winning for Black.

exercises.prompt: Why does getting a queen at nearly the same time not settle the result?
exercises.answer: White moves next and has checks that use Black’s king location and its own blocking pieces. The final result is a concrete mate rather than an automatic queen-ending draw.

startContext: Begin after ...Qxc6 at 76s in the saved seven-piece position. The preceding ten-piece rook and knight maneuvers and the larger queen-winning mistake remain source context. The promotion and dovetail finish are illustrated; the alternative queen block and wrong underpromotion are independently checked comparisons.
